ud1.10.text:
“Where water and earth,
fire and air have no footing—
there no star does shine,
nor does the sun shed its light;
there the moon glows not,
yet no darkness is found.
And when a sage, a brahmin, finds understanding
through their own sagacity,
then, from forms and formless,
from pleasure and pain they are released.”
ud1.10.title: With Bāhiya

ud1.1.text:
“When things become clear
to the keen, meditating brahmin,
his doubts are dispelled,
since he understands each thing and its cause.”
ud1.1.title: Upon Awakening (1st)

ud1.2.text:
“When things become clear
to the keen, meditating brahmin,
his doubts are dispelled,
since he’s known the end of conditions.”
ud1.2.title: Upon Awakening (2nd)

ud1.3.text:
“When things become clear
to the keen, meditating brahmin,
he remains, scattering Māra’s army,
as the sun lights up the sky.”
ud1.3.title: Upon Awakening (3rd)

ud1.4.text: “Any brahmin who has banished bad qualities— not murmuring the mystic syllable huṁ, unstained, self-controlled, a complete knowledge master who has completed the spiritual journey— they may legitimately proclaim the divine doctrine; who have no pretensions about anything in the world.”
ud1.4.title: The Mystic Syllable Huṁ

ud1.5.text:
“Having banished bad qualities,
those who live always mindful,
with fetters ended, awakened,
they are the world’s true brahmins.”
ud1.5.title: The Brahmin

ud1.6.text:
“The stranger, providing for no other,
tamed, consolidated in the core,
with defilements ended and flaws purged:
that’s who I declare a brahmin.”
ud1.6.title: With Mahākassapa

ud1.7.text:
“When a brahmin gets over
their own issues,
they transcend this goblin
and his havoc.”
ud1.7.title: At Ajakalāpaka

ud1.8.text:
“When she came he was not glad,
when she left he did not grieve.
Victorious in battle, freed from chains,
that’s who I declare a brahmin.”
ud1.8.title: With Saṅgāmaji

ud1.9.text:
“Purity doesn’t come from water,
no matter how many people bathe there.
One who has truth and principle,
they are pure, they are brahmins.”
ud1.9.title: Matted Hair Ascetics

ud2.10.text:
“They who hide no anger within,
passed beyond any kind of existence;
happy, free from fear and sorrow—
even the gods can’t see them.”
ud2.10.title: With Bhaddiya

ud2.1.text:
“Seclusion is happiness for the contented
who see the teaching they have learned.
Kindness for the world is happiness
for one who’d not harm a living creature.
Dispassion for the world is happiness
for one who has gone beyond sensual pleasures.
But dispelling the conceit ‘I am’
is truly the ultimate happiness.”
ud2.1.title: With Mucalinda

ud2.2.text:
“Neither the pleasures of the senses,
nor even divine happiness,
is worth even a sixteenth part
of the happiness of craving’s end.”
ud2.2.title: Kings

ud2.3.text:
“Creatures love happiness,
so if you harm them with a stick
in search of your own happiness,
after death you’ll find no happiness.
Creatures love happiness,
so if you don’t harm them with a stick
in search of your own happiness,
after death you will find happiness.”
ud2.3.title: A Stick

ud2.4.text:
“When struck by pleasure and pain <j>in the village or wilderness,
regard it not as self or alien.
Contacts strike because of attachment;
how would contacts strike one free of attachment?”
ud2.4.title: Esteem

ud2.5.text:
“One who has nothing is happy indeed,
a learned person who has appraised the teaching.
See how troubled are those with attachments,
a person bound tight to people.”
ud2.5.title: A Lay Follower

ud2.6.text:
“Oh! How happy are those with nothing!
Hence knowledge masters are people with nothing.
See how troubled are those with attachments,
a person bound tight to people.”
ud2.6.title: The Pregnant Woman

ud2.7.text:
“Hosts of gods and most human beings are bound
to what seems dear and pleasant.
Gloomy and exhausted,
they fall under the sway of the King of Death.
The diligent, who day and night
give up what seems pleasant,
dig out the root of gloom—
Death’s bait so hard to escape.”
ud2.7.title: An Only Son

ud2.8.text:
“Pain in the guise of pleasure,
the disliked in the guise of the liked,
suffering in the guise of happiness,
overpower the negligent.”
ud2.8.title: Suppavāsā

ud2.9.text:
“All under another’s control is suffering,
all under one’s own authority is pleasing;
what’s shared is stressful for both parties,
for yokes are hard to escape.”
ud2.9.title: With Visākhā

ud3.1.text:
“A mendicant who has left all deeds behind,
shaking off the dust of past deeds,
unselfish, steady, unaffected,
has no need to complain.”
ud3.1.title: Born of the Fruits of Deeds

ud3.2.text:
“The mendicant who has crossed over the bog,
who has crushed the thorn of sensuality,
who has reached the end of delusion,
trembles not at pleasure and pain.”
ud3.2.title: With Nanda

ud3.3.text:
“A mendicant who has beaten <j>the thorn of sensuality—
and abuse, killing, and caging—
steady as a mountain, imperturbable,
trembles not at pleasure and pain.”
ud3.3.title: With Yasoja

ud3.4.text:
“As a rocky mountain
is unwavering and well grounded,
so when delusion ends,
a monk, like a mountain, doesn’t tremble.”
ud3.4.title: With Sāriputta

ud3.5.text:
“With mindfulness of the body established,
restrained in the six fields of contact,
a mendicant always immersed in samādhi
would know extinguishment in themselves.”
ud3.5.title: With Mahāmoggallāna

ud3.6.text:
“In whom dwells no deceit or conceit,
rid of greed, unselfish, <j>with no need for hope,
with anger cast aside, quenched:
they are a brahmin, an ascetic, a mendicant.”
ud3.6.title: With Pilindavaccha

ud3.7.text:
“A mendicant who relies on alms,
self-supported, providing for no other;
the unaffected one is envied by even the gods,
calm and ever mindful.”
ud3.7.title: Sakka’s Heartfelt Saying

ud3.8.text:
“A mendicant who relies on alms,
self-supported, providing for no other;
the unaffected one is envied by even the gods,
but not if they’re after popularity and reputation.”
ud3.8.title: One Who Eats Only Almsfood

ud3.9.text:
“Living without a craft, light, wanting what is best,
with senses controlled, everywhere free;
a migrant with no bastion, unselfish, <j>with no need for hope,
having given up conceit, wandering alone: <j>that is a mendicant.”
ud3.9.title: Professions

ud4.10.text:
“With mind at peace, so full of peace,
for a mendicant who has cut the cord,
transmigration through births is finished:
they’re freed from Māra’s bonds.”
ud4.10.title: The Peacefulness of Sāriputta

ud4.1.text:
“Lesser thoughts and subtle thoughts
arise, springing up in the mind.
Not understanding these thoughts,
one with mind astray runs from one thing to the next.
Having understood these thoughts
that arise, springing up in the mind,
an awakened one—keen, restrained, and mindful—
has given them up without remainder.”
ud4.1.title: With Meghiya

ud4.2.text:
“Unguarded in body,
ruined by wrong view,
overcome with dullness and drowsiness,
you fall under Māra’s sway.
That’s why you should guard the mind,
with right thoughts your habitat,
and right view at the fore.
Having understood rise and fall,
a mendicant who has overcome <j>dullness and drowsiness
would abandon all bad destinies.”
ud4.2.title: Restless

ud4.3.text:
“A wrongly directed mind
would do you more harm
than a hater to the hated,
or an enemy to their foe.”
ud4.3.title: The Cowherd

ud4.4.text:
“One whose mind is like a rock,
steady, never shaking,
free of desire for desirable things,
not getting annoyed when things are annoying:
from where will suffering strike one
whose mind is developed like this?”
ud4.4.title: The Spirit’s Blow

ud4.5.text:
“The giant elephant,
with tusks like draft-poles,
agrees heart to heart with the spiritual giant,
since each finds joy in the woods alone.”
ud4.5.title: A Bull Elephant

ud4.6.title: The Alms-Gatherer

ud4.7.text:
“A sage of higher consciousness, diligent,
training in the ways of sagacity:
there are no sorrows for the unaffected,
calm and ever mindful.”
ud4.7.title: With Sāriputta

ud4.8.text:
“People out of control stab with words,
like they stab a tusker in battle with darts.
When they hear a harsh word spoken,
a mendicant should endure with no anger in heart.”
ud4.8.title: With Sundarī

ud4.9.text:
“One who has no guilt in life,
nor grief at facing death:
that attentive one who has seen the truth,
grieves not among the grieving.
For the mendicant with peaceful mind,
who has cut off craving for continued existence,
transmigration through births is finished,
there’ll be no more future lives for them.”
ud4.9.title: With Upasena

ud5.10.text:
“Steady in body, steady in mind,
standing, sitting or lying down:
a mendicant focusing on this mindfulness
gains an ever higher distinction.
And when they have done so,
they vanish from the King of Death.”
ud5.10.title: With Cūḷapanthaka

ud5.1.text:
“Having explored every quarter with the mind,
one finds no one dearer than oneself.
Likewise for others, each holds themselves dear;
so one who desires self-knowledge <j>would harm no other.”
ud5.1.title: Who is More Dear?

ud5.2.text:
“Whether born or to be born,
all depart, leaving the body behind.
The skillful, understanding that all is lost,
would keenly practice the spiritual life.”
ud5.2.title: Short-lived

ud5.3.text:
“As a clear-eyed man would avoid rough paths,
so long as strength is found;
an astute person in the living world,
would shun bad deeds.”
ud5.3.title: With Suppabuddha the Leper

ud5.4.text:
“If you fear pain,
if you dislike pain,
don’t do bad deeds
either openly or in secret.
If you should do a bad deed,
now or in the future,
you won’t be freed from suffering,
though you fly away and flee.”
ud5.4.title: The Boys

ud5.5.text:
“The rain saturates things that are covered up;
it doesn’t saturate things that are open.
Therefore you should open up a covered thing,
so the rain will not saturate it.”
ud5.5.title: Sabbath

ud5.6.text:
“Seeing the danger of the world,
I understood the truth without attachments.
The Noble One does not delight in evil,
the Pure One does not delight in evil.”
ud5.6.title: With Soṇa

ud5.7.text:
“Any doubts about this life or the next,
about one’s own experiences or those of another:
those who meditate give them all up,
keenly practicing the spiritual life.”
ud5.7.title: With Revata the Doubter

ud5.8.text:
“It’s easy for the good to do good,
but for the bad, doing good is hard.
For the bad, it’s easy to do bad,
but for the noble ones, doing bad is hard.”
ud5.8.title: Schism in the Saṅgha

ud5.9.text:
“Dolts pretending to be astute,
they talk, their words out of bounds.
They blab at will, their mouths agape,
and no one knows what leads them on.”
ud5.9.title: Teasing

ud6.1.text:
“Comparing the incomparable <j>with the creation of prolonged life,
the sage surrendered the life force.
Happy inside, serene,
he shattered self-creation like a suit of armor.”
ud6.1.title: Surrendering the Life Force

ud6.2.text:
“Don’t strive in every situation,
don’t become another’s man.
Don’t live depending on another,
and don’t use the teaching to make money.”
ud6.2.title: Seven Matted-Hair Ascetics

ud6.3.text:
“What was before then was not;
what before was not then was.
It never was, nor will it be,
nor is it found today.”
ud6.3.title: The Buddha’s Reviewing

ud6.4.text:
“Some ascetics and brahmins, it seems,
cling to these things.
Arguing, they dispute,
the folk who see just one part.”
ud6.4.title: Followers of Various Other Religions (1st)

ud6.5.text:
“Some ascetics and brahmins, it seems,
cling to these things.
They founder in mid-stream,
without reaching that objective.”
ud6.5.title: Followers of Various Other Religions (2nd)

ud6.7.text:
“In whom mental vibrations are cleared away,
internally clipped off entirely,
perceiving the formless, beyond chains,
having overcome the four yokes, <j>they never return.”
ud6.7.title: With Subhūti

ud6.9.text:
“Hastening by, they miss the essence,
sprouting ever more new bonds.
Like moths falling in the flame,
some have become fixed in what is seen or heard.”
ud6.9.title: Hastening By

ud7.10.text:
“The world is caught up in delusion,
but is looked on as making sense.
The fool caught up in attachment
is surrounded by darkness.
It seems as if eternal,
but for one who sees, there is nothing.”
ud7.10.title: King Udena

ud7.1.text:
“Above, below, everywhere free,
not contemplating ‘I am this’.
Freed like this, he has crossed the flood
not crossed before, so as to not be reborn.”
ud7.1.title: Bhaddiya the Dwarf (1st)

ud7.2.text:
“They’ve cut the cycle, gone to the wishless;
the streams are dried, they flow no more.
Cut, the cycle no longer spins.
Just this is the end of suffering.”
ud7.2.title: Bhaddiya the Dwarf (2nd)

ud7.3.text:
“Clinging to sensual pleasures, <j>to the chains of the senses,
blind to the faults of the fetters,
clinging to the chain of the fetters,
they’ll never cross the flood so vast.”
ud7.3.title: Clinging (1st)

ud7.4.text:
“Blinded by sensual pleasures, wrapped in a net,
they are smothered over by craving;
bound by the kinsman of the negligent,
like a fish caught in a funnel-net trap.
They chase old age and death,
like a suckling calf its mother.”
ud7.4.title: Clinging (2nd)

ud7.5.text:
“With faultless parts and white canopy,
the one-spoked chariot rolls on.
See it come, untroubled,
with stream cut, unbound.”
ud7.5.title: Another Discourse with Bhaddiya the Dwarf

ud7.6.text:
“There is no root or ground or leaves for them,
so where would creepers sprout from?
That attentive one is released from bonds:
who is worthy to criticize them?
Even the gods praise them,
and by the Divinity, too, they’re praised.”
ud7.6.title: The Ending of Craving

ud7.7.text:
“There is no proliferation remaining in those
who have passed beyond the halter and cross-bar.
The sage who lives without craving
is never scorned by the world with its gods.”
ud7.7.title: The Ending of Proliferation

ud7.8.text:
“Their mindfulness would always
be established in the body, constant:
‘It might not be, and it might not be mine,
It will not be, and it will not be mine.’
Meditating stage by stage on that,
in time they’d cross over clinging.”
ud7.8.title: Kaccāna

ud7.9.text:
“What difference would a well make
if water is there all the time?
Having cut off craving at the root,
who would go out on a quest?”
ud7.9.title: The Well

ud8.10.text:
“Just as the glow of iron struck
by a hammer in the fire of Jātaveda
gradually dissipates,
its destiny unknown;
in the same way, for the rightly released,
who have crossed the flood of sensual bonds,
there is no destination to describe—
they have found unshakable happiness.”
ud8.10.title: Dabba (2nd)

ud8.2.text:
“It’s hard to see what they call the ‘uninclined’,
for the truth is not easy to see.
For one who has penetrated craving,
who knows and sees, there is nothing.”
ud8.2.title: About Extinguishment (2nd)

ud8.5.text:
“A giver’s merit grows;
enmity doesn’t build up when you have self-control.
A skillful person gives up bad things—
with the end of greed, hate, and delusion, <j>they’re quenched.”
ud8.5.title: With Cunda

ud8.6.text:
“Those who cross a deluge or stream
have built a bridge and left the marshes behind.
While some people are still tying a raft,
intelligent people have crossed over.”
ud8.6.title: The Layfolk of Pāṭali Village

ud8.7.text:
“Walking together, dwelling as one,
the knowledge master mixes with foolish folk.
Knowing this, they give up wickedness,
like a milk-drinking heron the water.”
ud8.7.title: A Fork in the Road

ud8.9.text:
“The body is broken up, perception has ceased,
all feelings have become cool;
choices are stilled,
and consciousness come to an end.”
ud8.9.title: With Dabba (1st)

iti10.text:
“When overcome by hate
beings go to a bad place.
Having rightly understood that hate,
the discerning give it up.
Once they’ve given it up,
they never return to this world.”
iti10.title: Complete Understanding of Hate

iti7.text:
“Those who know the all as all,
are not attracted to anything.
They completely understand all,
and have risen above all suffering.”
iti7.title: Complete Understanding of All

iti8.text:
“These folk are caught up in conceit,
tied by conceit, delighting in existence.
Not completely understanding conceit,
they return in future lives.
Those who have given up conceit,
freed with the ending of conceit,
vanquishers of the tie of conceit,
have risen above all suffering.”
iti8.title: Complete Understanding of Conceit

iti94.text:
“For one who has given up seven chains,
a mendicant who has cut the cord,
transmigration through births is finished,
there’ll be no more future lives for them.”
iti94.title: Examination

iti99.text:
“One who knows their past lives,
sees heaven and places of loss,
and has attained the end of rebirth,
is a sage of perfect insight.
Because of these three knowledges
a brahmin is a master of the three knowledges.
That’s who I call a three-knowledge master,
and not the other <j>who repeats what they are told.”
iti99.title: The Three Knowledges

iti100.text:
“The Realized One, <j>compassionate for all living creatures,
unstintingly offers teaching.
Sentient beings revere him, <j>first among gods and humans,
who has gone beyond rebirth.”
iti100.title: The Brahmin’s Offering of the Teaching

iti101.text:
“When one is content with what’s blameless,
trifling, and easy to find,
they don’t get distressed
about lodgings, robes,
food, and drink,
and they’re not obstructed anywhere.
These qualities are said to be
integral to the ascetic life.
They’re mastered by a mendicant,
content and diligent.”
iti101.title: Easy to Find

iti102.text:
“As a trainee trains,
following the straight road,
first they know about ending;
enlightenment follows in the same lifetime.
Then to one freed through enlightenment
the knowledge of ending arises,
the supreme knowledge of freedom,
with the ending of the fetters.
Not by the lazy,
or by fools who don’t understand
may this be realized—extinguishment,
the release from all ties.”
iti102.title: The Ending of Defilements

iti104.text:
“This is a reason for joy
for those who understand:
that is, those who are evolved,
the noble ones living righteously.
They illuminate the true teaching,
beacons beaming light,
the attentive ones bringing light,
clear-eyed ones with strife discarded.
Having heard their instruction,
the astute, understanding rightly,
directly know the ending of rebirth,
they come not back to future lives.”
iti104.title: Accomplished in Ethics

iti105.text:
“Craving is a person’s partner
as they transmigrate on this long journey.
They go from this state to another,
but don’t escape transmigration.
Knowing this danger,
that craving is the cause of suffering—
rid of craving, free of grasping,
a mendicant would wander mindful.”
iti105.title: The Arising of Craving

iti108.text:
“Those who are deceivers and flatterers, <j>pompous and fake,
insolent and scattered:
these don’t grow in the teaching
that was taught by the perfected Buddha.
But those who are genuine, not flatterers, attentive,
amenable, and serene:
these do grow in the teaching
that was taught by the perfected Buddha.”
iti108.title: Deceivers

iti109.text:
“In pain they’d give up sensual pleasures,
aspiring to the future sanctuary from the yoke.
With deep understanding and heart well freed,
they’d experience universal liberation.
That knowledge master <j>who has completed the spiritual journey,
and gone to the end of the world, <j>is called ‘one who has gone beyond’.”
iti109.title: A River

iti14.text:
“There is no other thing
that shrouds people like ignorance.
Veiled by delusion,
they transmigrate day and night.
Those who have given up delusion,
shattering the mass of darkness,
wander no more,
the root is not found in them.”
iti14.title: The Shroud of Ignorance

iti16.text:
“There is nothing so helpful
for a trainee mendicant
aspiring for the ultimate goal
as rational application of mind.
Striving rationally, a mendicant
attains the end of suffering.”
iti16.title: A Trainee (1st)

iti17.text:
“A mendicant with good friends
is reverential and respectful
when their friends are speaking,
aware and mindful.
Gradually they would attain
the ending of all fetters.”
iti17.title: A Trainee (2nd)

iti18.text:
“A schismatic remains for the eon
in a place of loss, in hell.
Taking a stand against the teaching,
favoring factions, they ruin their sanctuary.
After causing schism in a harmonious Saṅgha,
they burn in hell for an eon.”
iti18.title: Schism in the Saṅgha

iti19.text:
“A Saṅgha in harmony is happy,
as is support for those in harmony.
Taking a stand on the teaching,
favoring harmony, they ruin no sanctuary.
After creating harmony in the Saṅgha,
they rejoice in heaven for an eon.”
iti19.title: Harmony in the Saṅgha

iti22.text:
“One should practice only good deeds,
whose happy outcome stretches ahead.
Giving and moral conduct,
developing a mind of love:
having developed these
three things yielding happiness,
that astute one is reborn
in a happy, pleasing world.”
iti22.title: The Benefits of Love

iti23.text:
“The astute praise diligence
in making merit.
Being diligent, an astute person
secures both benefits:
the benefit in this life,
and in lives to come.
Attentive, comprehending the meaning,
they are said to be astute.”
iti23.title: Both Kinds of Benefit

iti25.text:
“When a personage, spurning the hereafter,
transgresses in just one thing—
lying—
there is no evil they would not do.”
iti25.title: Lying

iti28.text:
“Eye, ear, nose,
tongue, body, and likewise mind:
a mendicant who leaves these
sense doors unguarded—
immoderate in eating,
sense faculties unrestrained—
reaps suffering
both physical and mental.
Burning in body,
burning in mind,
by day or by night
such a person lives in suffering.”
iti28.title: Living in Suffering

iti30.text:
“Having done bad things
by way of body,
speech, and mind,
and whatever else is corrupt;
not having done good deeds,
and having done many bad,
when their body breaks up, that witless person
is reborn in hell.”
iti30.title: Mortifying

iti32.text:
“If a person possesses
these two qualities—
bad conduct
and bad views—
when their body breaks up, that witless person
is reborn in hell.”
iti32.title: Ethics (1st)

iti34.text:
“Neither keen nor prudent,
lazy, lacking energy,
full of dullness and drowsiness,
unconscientious, lacking regard for others,
such a mendicant is incapable
of experiencing the highest awakening.
One who is mindful, alert, meditative,
keen, prudent, and diligent,
having cut the fetter of birth and old age,
would experience supreme awakening <j>in this very life.”
iti34.title: Keen

iti35.text:
“The Buddha taught the spiritual life
not because of legends,
but for the sake of restraint and giving up,
and because its objective is extinguishment.
This is the path followed by the great souls,
the great seers.
Those who practice it
as it was taught by the Buddha
doing the Teacher’s bidding,
make an end of suffering.”
iti35.title: Fawning and Flattery

iti37.text:
“At inspiring places
an astute person should be inspired;
a keen and alert mendicant
should examine with wisdom.
A mendicant living like this, with keen energy,
peaceful not restless,
devoted to serenity of heart,
attains the ending of suffering.”
iti37.title: Happiness

iti39.text:
“See the two approaches for
explaining the Dhamma
used by the Realized One, the Buddha,
compassionate for all beings:
see that that is evil,
and be dispassionate toward it.
Then, with a mind free of desire,
you’ll make an end of suffering.”
iti39.title: Teaching

iti41.text:
“See the world with its gods,
bereft of wisdom,
habituated to name and form,
imagining this is truth.
Wisdom is best in the world,
as it leads to penetration,
through which one rightly understands
the ending of rebirth and continued existence.
Gods and humans envy them,
the Buddhas, ever mindful,
of laughing wisdom,
bearing their final body.”
iti41.title: Bereft of Wisdom

iti42.text:
“Those in whom conscience and prudence
are never found at all,
have lost their bright roots,
and fare on in birth and death.
Those in whom conscience and prudence
are always rightly established,
thrive in the spiritual life;
being at peace, they will not be reborn again.”
iti42.title: Bright Things

iti45.text:
“With minds at peace, alert,
mindful and meditative,
they rightly discern the Dhamma,
unconcerned for sensual pleasures.
Delighting in diligence, peaceful,
seeing fear in negligence,
such a one can’t decline,
and has drawn near to extinguishment.”
iti45.title: Retreat

iti46.text:
“The training fulfilled, not liable to decline,
overseen by wisdom, seer of rebirth’s end;
that sage bears their final body;
they have disposed of Māra, I declare, <j>and gone beyond old age.
Therefore be always enjoying absorption, <j>immersed in samādhi,
energetic, seers of rebirth’s end.
Having overcome Māra and his armies, mendicants,
go beyond birth and death.”
iti46.title: The Benefits of Training

iti50.text:
“When greed, hate, and delusion,
have arisen inside oneself,
they harm a person of wicked heart,
as a bamboo is destroyed by its own fruit.”
iti50.title: Roots

iti51.text:
“Comprehending the realm of luminous form,
not stuck in the formless,
those who are released in cessation,
they are conquerors of death.
Having directly experienced <j>the element free of death,
free of attachments;
having realized relinquishment
of attachments, the undefiled
fully awakened Buddha teaches
the sorrowless, stainless state.”
iti51.title: Elements

iti52.text:
“Stilled, aware,
a mindful disciple of the Buddha
understands feelings,
the cause of feelings,
where they cease,
and the path that leads to their ending.
With the ending of feelings, a mendicant
is hungerless, quenched.”
iti52.title: Feelings (1st)

iti53.text:
“A mendicant who sees pleasure as pain,
and suffering as a dart,
and that peaceful, neutral feeling
as impermanent
sees rightly.
And when freed in regards to that,
that peaceful sage, with perfect insight,
has truly slipped their yokes.”
iti53.title: Feelings (2nd)

iti57.text:
“One who has ended the defilement of sensuality,
whose ignorance has faded away,
and whose desire to be reborn is finished—
liberated, free of attachments,
they bear their final body,
having vanquished Māra with his legions.”
iti57.title: Defilements (2nd)

iti59.text:
“Whoever has well developed
ethics, immersion, and wisdom
has slipped free of Māra’s dominion
and dazzles like the sun.”
iti59.title: Māra’s Dominion

iti61.text:
“The eye of flesh, the clairvoyant eye,
the supreme eye of wisdom:
these three eyes
were taught by the supreme person.
The arising of the eye of flesh
is the path to the clairvoyant eye.
When knowledge arises—
the supreme eye of wisdom—
one who gains that eye
is released from all suffering.”
iti61.title: The Eye

iti66.text:
“Purity of body, purity of speech,
and undefiled purity of heart.
A pure one, blessed with purity,
has given up everything, they say.”
iti66.title: Purity

iti67.text:
“A sage in body, a sage in speech,
a sage undefiled in mind;
a sage, blessed with sagacity,
has washed off all bad things, they say.”
iti67.title: Sagacity

iti68.text:
“Those in whom greed, hate, and ignorance
have faded away,
belong with those who are evolved;
A manifestation of divinity, realized,
awakened, beyond enmities and fears,
they’ve given up everything, they say.”
iti68.title: Greed (1st)

iti70.text:
“When the mind has been misdirected,
and words wrongly spoken,
and wrong bodily deeds have been done,
an individual here
unlearned, doer of bad deeds,
though their life may be short,
when their body breaks up, that witless person
is reborn in hell.”
iti70.title: Having Wrong View

iti72.text:
“Knowing the escape from sensuality,
and form’s transcendence,
one always keen touches
the stilling of all activities.
That mendicant sees rightly,
and when freed in regards to that,
that peaceful sage, with perfect insight,
has truly slipped their yoke.”
iti72.title: Elements of Escape

iti74.text:
“The astute wish for a child
who betters or equals their birth;
not one who fails their birth,
disgracing their family.
These are the children in the world
who become lay devotees;
faithful, accomplished in ethics,
bountiful, rid of stinginess.
Like the moon freed from clouds,
they dazzle in the assemblies.”
iti74.title: A Child

iti77.text:
“Knowing that the body is fragile,
that consciousness is faded,
and seeing the danger in attachments,
they go beyond birth and death.
Having attained ultimate peace,
evolved, they await their time.”
iti77.title: Fragile

iti79.text:
“Restless, they relish
work, talk, and sleep.
Such a mendicant is incapable
of experiencing the highest awakening.
That’s why one ought have few duties,
being wakeful not restless.
Such a mendicant is capable
of experiencing the highest awakening.”
iti79.title: Decline

iti80.text:
“One concerned with being looked up to,
with possessions, honor, and respect,
with sharing joys with friends,
is far from the ending of fetters.
But one who gives up children and herds,
marriage and acquisitions—
such a mendicant is capable
of experiencing the highest awakening.”
iti80.title: Thoughts

iti81.text:
“Whether they’re honored
or not honored, or both,
their immersion doesn’t waver
as they abide in the immeasurables.
They persistently practice absorption
with subtle view and discernment.
Rejoicing in the ending of grasping,
they’re said to be a true person.”
iti81.title: Esteem

iti86.text:
“Delighting in the teaching, enjoying the teaching,
contemplating the teaching,
a mendicant who recollects the teaching
doesn’t fall away from the true teaching.
Whether walking or standing,
sitting or lying down,
with mind collected inside,
they attain only peace.”
iti86.title: Practicing In Line With the Teaching

iti87.text:
“Think the three skillful thoughts,
and get rid of the unskillful.
Quelling such thoughts and considerations,
like rain on the dust,
with a heart calmed of thought,
you’ll touch the state of peace right here.”
iti87.title: Destroyers of Sight

dhp1.text:
Intention is the leader of things;
intention is first, they’re made by intention.
If with corrupt intent
you speak or act,
suffering follows you,
like a wheel, the ox’s foot.
dhp1.title: 1. Pairs

dhp3.text:
“They abused me, they hit me!
They beat me, they robbed me!”
For those who bear such a grudge,
hatred is never laid to rest.
dhp3.title: dhp3

dhp5.text:
For never is hatred
laid to rest by hate,
it’s laid to rest by love:
this is an ancient teaching.
dhp5.title: dhp5

dhp6.title: dhp6

dhp7.text:
Those who contemplate the beautiful,
their faculties unrestrained,
immoderate in eating,
lazy, lacking energy:
Māra strikes them down
like the wind, a feeble tree.
dhp7.title: dhp7

dhp8.text:
Those who contemplate the ugly,
their faculties well-restrained,
eating in moderation,
faithful and energetic:
Māra cannot strike them down,
like the wind, a rocky mountain.
dhp8.title: dhp8

dhp9.text:
One who, not free of stains themselves,
would wear the robe stained in ocher,
bereft of self-control and truth:
they are not worthy of the ocher robe.
dhp9.title: dhp9

dhp10.text:
One who’s purged all their stains,
steady in ethics,
possessed of self-control and of truth,
they are truly worthy of the ocher robe.
dhp10.title: dhp10

dhp11.text:
Thinking the inessential is essential,
seeing the essential as inessential;
they don’t realize the essential,
for wrong thoughts are their habitat.
dhp11.title: dhp11

dhp12.text:
Having known the essential as essential,
and the inessential as inessential;
they realize the essential,
for right thoughts are their habitat.
dhp12.title: dhp12

dhp13.text:
Just as rain seeps into
a poorly roofed house,
lust seeps into
an undeveloped mind.
dhp13.title: dhp13

dhp14.text:
Just as rain doesn’t seep into
a well roofed house,
lust doesn’t seep into
a well developed mind.
dhp14.title: dhp14

dhp15.text:
Here they grieve, hereafter they grieve,
an evildoer grieves in both places.
They grieve and fret,
seeing their own corrupt deeds.
dhp15.title: dhp15

dhp16.text:
Here they rejoice, hereafter they rejoice,
one who does good rejoices in both places.
They rejoice and celebrate,
seeing their own pure deeds.
dhp16.title: dhp16

dhp17.text:
Here they’re tormented, <j>hereafter they’re tormented,
an evildoer is tormented in both places.
They’re tormented <j>thinking of bad things they’ve done;
when gone to a bad place, <j>they’re tormented all the more.
dhp17.title: dhp17

dhp18.text:
Here they delight, hereafter they delight,
one who does good delights in both places.
They delight thinking of good things they’ve done;
when gone to a good place, they delight all the more.
dhp18.title: dhp18

dhp19.text:
Much though they may recite scripture,
if a negligent person does not apply them,
then, like a cowherd who counts the cattle of others,
they miss out on the blessings of the ascetic life.
dhp19.title: dhp19

dhp20.text:
Little though they may recite scripture,
if they live in line with the teaching,
having given up greed, hate, and delusion,
with deep understanding and heart well freed,
not grasping to this life or the next,
they share in the blessings of the ascetic life.
dhp20.title: dhp20

dhp100.text:
Better than a thousand
meaningless sayings
is a single meaningful saying,
hearing which brings you peace.
dhp100.title: 8. The Thousands

dhp102.text:
Better than reciting
a hundred meaningless verses
is a single saying of Dhamma,
hearing which brings you peace.
dhp102.title: dhp102

dhp103.text:
The supreme conqueror is
not he who conquers a million men in battle,
but he who conquers a single man:
himself.
dhp103.title: dhp103

dhp104.text:
It is surely better to conquer oneself
than all those other folk.
When a person has tamed themselves,
always living restrained,
dhp104.title: dhp104

dhp105.text:
no god nor centaur,
nor Māra nor divinity,
can undo the victory
of such a personage.
dhp105.title: dhp105

dhp106.text:
Rather than a thousandfold sacrifice,
every month for a full century,
it’s better to honor for a single hour
one who has developed themselves.
That offering is better
than the hundred year sacrifice.
dhp106.title: dhp106

dhp108.text:
Whatever sacrifice or offering in the world
a seeker of merit may make for a year,
none of it is worth a quarter
of bowing to the sincere.
dhp108.title: dhp108

dhp109.text:
For one in the habit of bowing,
always honoring the elders,
four blessings grow:
lifespan, beauty, happiness, and strength.
dhp109.title: dhp109

dhp110.text:
Better to live a single day
ethical and absorbed in meditation
than to live a hundred years
unethical and lacking immersion.
dhp110.title: dhp110

dhp112.text:
Better to live a single day
energetic and strong,
than to live a hundred years
lazy and lacking energy.
dhp112.title: dhp112

dhp113.text:
Better to live a single day
seeing rise and fall
than to live a hundred years
blind to rise and fall.
dhp113.title: dhp113

dhp114.text:
Better to live a single day
seeing the state free of death
than to live a hundred years
blind to the state free of death.
dhp114.title: dhp114

dhp116.title: 9. Wickedness

dhp117.text:
If you do something bad,
don’t do it again and again,
don’t set your heart on it,
for piling up evil is suffering.
dhp117.title: dhp117

dhp119.text:
Even the wicked see good things,
so long as their wickedness has not ripened.
But as soon as that wickedness ripens,
then the wicked see wicked things.
dhp119.title: dhp119

dhp121.text:
Think not lightly of evil,
that it won’t come back to you.
The pot is filled with water
falling drop by drop;
the fool is filled with wickedness
piled up bit by bit.
dhp121.title: dhp121

dhp123.text:
Avoid wickedness,
as a merchant with rich cargo and small escort
would avoid a dangerous road,
or one who loves life would avoid drinking poison.
dhp123.title: dhp123

dhp124.title: dhp124

dhp125.text:
Whoever wrongs a man who has done no wrong,
a pure man who has not a blemish,
the evil backfires on the fool,
like fine dust thrown upwind.
dhp125.title: dhp125

dhp126.title: dhp126

dhp127.text:
Not in midair, nor mid-ocean,
nor hiding in a mountain cleft;
you’ll find no place on the planet
to escape your wicked deeds.
dhp127.title: dhp127

dhp128.text:
Not in midair, nor mid-ocean,
nor hiding in a mountain cleft;
you’ll find no place on the planet
where you won’t be vanquished by death.
dhp128.title: dhp128

dhp129.text:
All tremble at the rod,
all fear death.
Treating others like oneself,
neither kill nor incite to kill.
dhp129.title: 10. The Rod

dhp133.text:
Don’t speak harshly,
they may speak harshly back.
For aggressive speech is painful,
and the rod may spring back on you.
dhp133.title: dhp133

dhp134.text:
If you still yourself
like a broken gong,
you reach extinguishment
and know no conflict.
dhp134.title: dhp134

dhp135.text:
As a cowherd drives the cows
to pasture with the rod,
so too old age and death
drive life from living beings.
dhp135.title: dhp135

dhp136.text:
The fool does not understand
the evil that they do.
But because of those deeds, that simpleton
is tormented as if burnt by fire.
dhp136.title: dhp136

dhp137.text:
One who violently attacks
the peaceful and the innocent
swiftly falls
to one of ten bad states:
dhp137.title: dhp137

dhp138.title: dhp138

dhp139.title: dhp139

dhp140.text:
or else their home
is consumed by fire.
When their body breaks up, that witless person
is reborn in hell.
dhp140.title: dhp140

dhp141.text:
Not nudity, nor matted hair, nor mud,
nor fasting, nor lying on bare ground,
nor wearing dust and dirt, or squatting on the heels,
will cleanse a mortal not free of doubt.
dhp141.title: dhp141

dhp142.text:
Dressed up they may be, but if they live well—
peaceful, tamed, committed to the spiritual path,
having laid aside violence toward all creatures—
they are a brahmin, an ascetic, a mendicant.
dhp142.title: dhp142

dhp143.text:
Can a person constrained by conscience
be found in the world?
Who shies away from blame,
like a fine horse from the whip?
dhp143.title: dhp143

dhp144.text:
Like a fine horse under the whip,
be keen and full of urgency.
With faith, ethics, and energy,
immersion, and investigation of principles,
accomplished in knowledge and conduct, mindful,
give up this vast suffering.
dhp144.title: dhp144

dhp145.text:
While irrigators guide water,
fletchers bend arrows straight,
and carpenters bend timber straight,
those true to their vows tame themselves.
dhp145.title: dhp145

dhp146.text:
What is joy, what is laughter,
when the flames are ever burning?
Swathed in darkness,
would you not seek a light?
dhp146.title: 11. Old Age

dhp147.text:
See this fancy puppet,
a body built of sores,
diseased, obsessed over,
in which nothing lasts at all.
dhp147.title: dhp147

dhp148.text:
This body is decrepit and frail,
a nest of disease.
This foul carcass falls apart,
for life ends in death.
dhp148.title: dhp148

dhp149.text:
These dove-grey bones
are tossed away like
dried gourds in the autumn—
what joy is there in such a sight?
dhp149.title: dhp149

dhp150.text:
In this city built of bones,
plastered with flesh and blood,
old age and death are stashed away,
along with conceit and contempt.
dhp150.title: dhp150

dhp151.text:
Fancy chariots of kings wear out,
and even this body gets old.
But the truth of the good never gets old—
so the good proclaim to the good.
dhp151.title: dhp151

dhp152.text:
A person of little learning
ages like an ox—
their flesh grows,
but not their wisdom.
dhp152.title: dhp152

dhp153.text:
Transmigrating through countless rebirths,
I’ve journeyed without reward,
searching for the house-builder;
painful is birth again and again.
dhp153.title: dhp153

dhp154.text:
I’ve seen you, house-builder!
You won’t build a house again!
Your rafters are all broken,
your roof-peak demolished.
The mind, set on demolition,
has reached the end of cravings.
dhp154.title: dhp154

dhp155.text:
When young they spurned the spiritual path
and failed to earn any wealth.
Now they brood like old cranes
in a pond bereft of fish.
dhp155.title: dhp155

dhp156.text:
When young they spurned the spiritual path
and failed to earn any wealth.
Now they lie like spent arrows,
bemoaning over things past.
dhp156.title: dhp156

dhp157.text:
If you knew your self as beloved,
you’d look after it so well.
In one of the night’s three watches,
an astute person would remain alert.
dhp157.title: 12. The Self

dhp158.text:
The astute would avoid being corrupted
by first grounding themselves
in what is suitable,
and then instructing others.
dhp158.title: dhp158

dhp159.text:
If one were to treat oneself
as one instructs another,
the well-tamed indeed would tame:
for the self, it seems, is hard to tame.
dhp159.title: dhp159

dhp160.text:
One is indeed the lord of oneself,
for who else would be one’s lord?
By means of a well-tamed self,
one gains a lord that’s rare indeed.
dhp160.title: dhp160

dhp161.text:
For the evil that is done by oneself,
born and produced in oneself,
grinds down a simpleton,
as diamond grinds a lesser gem.
dhp161.title: dhp161

dhp162.text:
One choked by immorality,
as a sal tree by a creeper,
does to themselves
what a foe only wishes.
dhp162.title: dhp162

dhp163.text:
It’s easy to do bad things
harmful to oneself,
but good things that are helpful
are the hardest things to do.
dhp163.title: dhp163

dhp164.text:
On account of wicked views—
scorning the guidance
of the perfected ones,
the noble ones living righteously—
the idiot begets their own self’s demise,
like the bamboo bearing fruit.
dhp164.title: dhp164

dhp165.text:
For it is by oneself that evil’s done,
one is corrupted by oneself.
It’s by oneself that evil’s not done,
one is purified by oneself.
Purity and impurity are personal matters,
no one can purify another.
dhp165.title: dhp165

dhp166.text:
Never neglect what is good for yourself
for the sake of another, however great.
Knowing well what is good for yourself,
be intent upon your heart’s goal.
dhp166.title: dhp166

dhp167.text:
Don’t resort to lowly things,
don’t abide in negligence,
don’t resort to wrong views,
don’t perpetuate the world.
dhp167.title: 13. The World

dhp168.text:
Get up, don’t be heedless,
live by principle, with good conduct.
For one of good conduct sleeps at ease,
in this world and the next.
dhp168.title: dhp168

dhp170.text:
Look upon the world
as a bubble
or a mirage,
then the King of Death won’t see you.
dhp170.title: dhp170

dhp171.text:
Come, see this world decked out
like a fancy royal chariot.
Here fools founder,
but the discerning are not chained.
dhp171.title: dhp171

dhp172.text:
He who once was heedless,
but turned to heedfulness,
shines upon this world
like the moon freed from clouds.
dhp172.title: dhp172

dhp173.text:
Someone whose bad deed
is supplanted by the good,
shines upon this world,
like the moon freed from clouds.
dhp173.title: dhp173

dhp174.text:
Blind is the world,
few are those who clearly see.
Only a handful go to heaven,
like a bird freed from a net.
dhp174.title: dhp174

dhp175.text:
Swans fly by the sun’s path,
psychic sages fly through space.
The attentive leave the world,
having vanquished Māra with his legions.
dhp175.title: dhp175

dhp177.text:
The miserly don’t ascend to heaven,
it takes a fool to not praise giving.
The attentive celebrate giving,
and so find happiness in the hereafter.
dhp177.title: dhp177

dhp178.text:
The fruit of stream-entry is better
than being the one king of the earth,
than going to heaven,
than lordship over all the world.
dhp178.title: dhp178

dhp179.text:
He whose victory may not be undone,
a victory unrivaled in all the world;
by what track would you trace that Buddha,
who leaves no track in his infinite range?
dhp179.title: 14. The Buddhas

dhp180.text:
Of craving, the weaver, the clinger, he has none:
so where can he be traced?
By what track would you trace that Buddha,
who leaves no track in his infinite range?
dhp180.title: dhp180

dhp181.text:
The attentive intent on absorption,
who love the peace of renunciation,
the Buddhas, ever mindful,
are envied by even the gods.
dhp181.title: dhp181

dhp182.title: dhp182

dhp183.title: dhp183

dhp184.text:
Patient acceptance is the ultimate fervor.
Extinguishment is the ultimate, say the Buddhas.
No true renunciate injures another,
nor does an ascetic hurt another.
dhp184.title: dhp184

dhp186.text:
Even if it were raining money,
you’d not be sated in sensual pleasures.
An astute person understands that sensual pleasures
offer little gratification and much suffering.
dhp186.title: dhp186

dhp187.text:
Thus they find no delight
even in celestial pleasures.
A disciple of the fully awakened Buddha
delights in the ending of craving.
dhp187.title: dhp187

dhp188.text:
So many go for refuge
to mountains and forest groves,
to shrines in tended parks;
those people are driven by fear.
dhp188.title: dhp188

dhp189.text:
But such refuge is no sanctuary,
it is no supreme refuge.
By going to that refuge,
you’re not released from all suffering.
dhp189.title: dhp189

dhp190.text:
One gone for refuge to the Buddha,
to his teaching and to the Saṅgha,
sees the four noble truths
with right understanding:
dhp190.title: dhp190

dhp191.text:
suffering, suffering’s origin,
suffering’s transcendence,
and the noble eightfold path
that leads to the stilling of suffering.
dhp191.title: dhp191

dhp193.text:
It’s hard to find a thoroughbred man:
they’re not born just anywhere.
A family where that attentive one is born
prospers in happiness.
dhp193.title: dhp193

dhp194.text:
Happy, the arising of Buddhas!
Happy, the teaching of Dhamma!
Happy is the harmony of the Saṅgha,
and the striving of the harmonious is happy.
dhp194.title: dhp194

dhp195.text:
When a person venerates the worthy—
the Buddha or his disciple,
who have transcended proliferation,
and have left behind grief and lamentation,
dhp195.title: dhp195

dhp196.text:
quenched, fearing nothing from any quarter—
the merit of one venerating such as these,
cannot be calculated by anyone,
saying it is just this much.
dhp196.title: dhp196

dhp197.text:
Let us live so very happily,
loving among the hostile.
Among hostile humans,
let us live with love.
dhp197.title: 15. Happiness

dhp198.text:
Let us live so very happily,
healthy among the ailing.
Among ailing humans
let us live healthily.
dhp198.title: dhp198

dhp200.text:
Let us live so very happily,
we who have nothing.
We shall feed on rapture,
like the gods of sublime luminosity.
dhp200.title: dhp200

dhp201.text:
Victory breeds enmity;
the defeated sleep badly.
The peaceful sleep at ease,
having left victory and defeat behind.
dhp201.title: dhp201

dhp202.text:
There is no fire like greed,
no crime like hate,
no suffering like the aggregates,
no bliss beyond peace.
dhp202.title: dhp202

dhp203.text:
Hunger is the worst illness,
conditions are the worst suffering.
When one has known this as it is,
extinguishment is the ultimate happiness.
dhp203.title: dhp203

dhp204.title: dhp204

dhp205.text:
Having drunk the nectar of seclusion
and the nectar of peace—
free of stress, free of evil,
drink the joyous nectar of truth.
dhp205.title: dhp205

dhp206.text:
It’s good to see the noble ones,
staying with them is always good.
Were you not to see fools,
you’d always be happy.
dhp206.title: dhp206

dhp207.text:
For one who consorts with fools
grieves long.
Painful is living with fools,
like being stuck with your enemy.
Happy is living with an attentive one,
like meeting with your kin.
dhp207.title: dhp207

dhp208.text:
Therefore:
An attentive one, wise and learned,
a behemoth of virtue, true to their vows, noble:
follow a true and intelligent person such as this,
as the moon tracks the path of the stars.
dhp208.title: dhp208

dhp209.text:
Applying yourself where you ought not,
neglecting what you should be doing,
forgetting your goal, you cling to what you hold dear,
jealous of those devoted to their heart’s goal.
dhp209.title: 16. The Beloved

dhp210.text:
Don’t ever get too close
to those you like or dislike.
For not seeing the liked is suffering,
and so is seeing the disliked.
dhp210.title: dhp210

dhp211.text:
Therefore don’t hold anything dear,
for it’s bad to lose those you love.
No ties are found in they who
hold nothing loved or loathed.
dhp211.title: dhp211

dhp212.text:
Sorrow springs from what we hold dear,
fear springs from what we hold dear;
one free from holding anything dear
has no sorrow, let alone fear.
dhp212.title: dhp212

dhp213.text:
Sorrow springs from attachment,
fear springs from attachment;
one free from attachment
has no sorrow, let alone fear.
dhp213.title: dhp213

dhp217.text:
One accomplished in virtue and vision,
firmly principled, and truthful,
doing oneself what ought be done:
that’s who the people love.
dhp217.title: dhp217

dhp218.text:
One eager to realize the ineffable
would be filled with awareness.
Their mind not bound to pleasures of sense,
they’re said to be heading upstream.
dhp218.title: dhp218

dhp219.text:
When a man returns safely
after a long time spent abroad,
family, friends, and loved ones
celebrate his return.
dhp219.title: dhp219

dhp220.text:
Just so, when one who has done good
goes from this world to the next,
their good deeds receive them there,
as family welcomes home one they love.
dhp220.title: dhp220

dhp21.text:
Heedfulness is the state free of death;
heedlessness is the state of death.
The heedful do not die,
while the heedless are like the dead.
dhp21.title: 2. Diligence

dhp22.text:
Understanding this distinction
when it comes to heedfulness,
the astute rejoice in heedfulness,
happy in the noble ones’ domain.
dhp22.title: dhp22

dhp23.text:
They who regularly meditate,
always staunchly vigorous;
the attentive realize extinguishment,
the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.
dhp23.title: dhp23

dhp24.text:
For the hard-working and mindful,
pure of deed and attentive,
restrained, living righteously, and diligent,
their reputation only grows.
dhp24.title: dhp24

dhp25.text:
By hard work and diligence,
by restraint and by self-control,
a smart person would build an island
that the floods cannot overflow.
dhp25.title: dhp25

dhp26.text:
Fools and simpletons
devote themselves to negligence.
But the wise protect diligence
as their best treasure.
dhp26.title: dhp26

dhp27.text:
Don’t devote yourself to negligence,
or delight in erotic intimacy.
For if you’re diligent and meditate,
you’ll attain abundant happiness.
dhp27.title: dhp27

dhp28.text:
When the astute dispel negligence
by means of diligence,
ascending the palace of wisdom,
sorrowless, they behold this generation of sorrow,
as an attentive one on a mountain top
beholds the fools below.
dhp28.title: dhp28

dhp29.text:
Heedful among the heedless,
wide awake while others sleep—
a true sage leaves them behind,
like a swift horse passing a feeble.
dhp29.title: dhp29

dhp30.text:
Maghavā became chief of the gods
by means of diligence.
People praise diligence,
while negligence is always deplored.
dhp30.title: dhp30

dhp31.text:
A mendicant who loves diligence,
seeing fear in negligence—
advances like fire,
burning up fetters big and small.
dhp31.title: dhp31

dhp32.text:
A mendicant who loves diligence,
seeing fear in negligence—
such a one can’t decline,
and has drawn near to extinguishment.
dhp32.title: dhp32

dhp221.text:
Give up anger, get rid of conceit,
and escape every fetter.
Sufferings don’t befall one who has nothing,
not clinging to name and form.
dhp221.title: 17. Anger

dhp222.text:
When anger surges like a lurching chariot,
keep it in check.
That’s what I call a charioteer;
others just hold the reins.
dhp222.title: dhp222

dhp223.text:
Defeat anger with kindness,
villainy with virtue,
stinginess with giving,
and lies with truth.
dhp223.title: dhp223

dhp224.text:
Speak the truth, do not be angry,
and give when asked, if only a little.
By these three means,
you may enter the presence of the gods.
dhp224.title: dhp224

dhp225.text:
Those harmless sages,
always restrained in body,
go to the state that does not pass,
where there is no sorrow.
dhp225.title: dhp225

dhp226.text:
Always wakeful,
practicing night and day,
focused only on extinguishment,
their defilements come to an end.
dhp226.title: dhp226

dhp227.text:
It’s always been this way, Atula,
it’s not just today.
They blame you when you’re silent,
they blame you when you speak a lot,
and even when you speak just right:
no one in the world escapes blame.
dhp227.title: dhp227

dhp228.text:
There never was, nor will be,
nor is there today,
someone who is wholly praised
or wholly blamed.
dhp228.title: dhp228

dhp229.text:
If, after watching them day in day out,
discerning people praise
that sage of impeccable conduct,
endowed with ethics and wisdom;
dhp229.title: dhp229

dhp230.text:
like a pendant of Black Plum River gold,
who is worthy to criticize them?
Even the gods praise them,
and by the Divinity, too, they’re praised.
dhp230.title: dhp230

dhp231.text:
Guard against ill-tempered deeds,
be restrained in body.
Giving up bad bodily conduct,
conduct yourself well in body.
dhp231.title: dhp231

dhp234.text:
An attentive one is restrained in body
restrained also in speech,
in thought, too, they are restrained:
they are restrained in every way.
dhp234.title: dhp234

dhp235.text:
Today you’re like a withered leaf,
Yama’s men await you.
You stand at the departure gates,
yet you have no supplies for the road.
dhp235.title: 18. Stains

dhp236.text:
Make an island of yourself!
Swiftly strive, learn to be wise!
Purged of stains, flawless,
you’ll go to the heavenly realm of the noble ones.
dhp236.title: dhp236

dhp237.text:
You’ve journeyed the stages of life,
and now you set out to meet Yama.
Along the way there’s nowhere to stay,
yet you have no supplies for the road.
dhp237.title: dhp237

dhp238.text:
Make an island of yourself!
Swiftly strive, learn to be wise!
Purged of stains, flawless,
you’ll not come again to rebirth and old age.
dhp238.title: dhp238

dhp239.text:
A smart person would purge
their own stains gradually,
bit by bit, moment by moment,
like a smith smelting silver.
dhp239.title: dhp239

dhp240.text:
It is the rust born on the iron
that eats away the place it arose.
And so it is their own deeds
that lead the overly-ascetic to a bad place.
dhp240.title: dhp240

dhp241.text:
Not rehearsing is the stain of hymns.
The stain of houses is neglect.
Laziness is the stain of beauty.
A guard’s stain is negligence.
dhp241.title: dhp241

dhp242.text:
Misconduct is a woman’s stain.
A giver’s stain is stinginess.
Bad qualities are a stain
in this world and the next.
dhp242.title: dhp242

dhp243.text:
But a worse stain than these
is ignorance, the worst stain of all.
Having given up that stain,
be without stains, mendicants!
dhp243.title: dhp243

dhp244.text:
Life is easy for the shameless.
With all the rude courage of a crow,
they live pushy,
rude, and corrupt.
dhp244.title: dhp244

dhp245.text:
Life is hard for the conscientious,
always seeking purity,
neither clinging nor rude,
pure of livelihood and discerning.
dhp245.title: dhp245

dhp246.text:
Take anyone in this world
who kills living creatures,
speaks falsely, steals,
commits adultery,
dhp246.title: dhp246

dhp247.text:
and indulges in drinking
beer and wine.
Right here they dig up
the root of their own self.
dhp247.title: dhp247

dhp248.text:
Know this, my man:
they are unrestrained and wicked.
Don’t let that greed and unrighteousness
inflict pain on you for long.
dhp248.title: dhp248

dhp249.text:
The people give according to their faith,
according to their confidence.
If you get upset over that,
over others’ food and drink,
you’ll not, by day or by night,
become immersed in samādhi.
dhp249.title: dhp249

dhp250.text:
Those who have cut that out,
dug it up at the root, eradicated it,
they will, by day or by night,
become immersed in samādhi.
dhp250.title: dhp250

dhp251.text:
There is no fire like greed,
no crime like hate,
no net like delusion,
no river like craving.
dhp251.title: dhp251

dhp252.text:
It’s easy to see the faults of others,
hard to see one’s own.
For the faults of others
are tossed high like hay,
while one’s own are hidden,
as a cheat hides a bad hand.
dhp252.title: dhp252

dhp253.text:
When you look for the flaws of others,
always finding fault,
your defilements only grow,
you’re far from ending defilements.
dhp253.title: dhp253

dhp254.text:
In the atmosphere there is no track,
there’s no true ascetic outside here.
People enjoy proliferation,
the Realized Ones are free of proliferation.
dhp254.title: dhp254

dhp255.text:
In the atmosphere there is no track,
there’s no true ascetic outside here.
No conditions last forever,
the Awakened Ones are not shaken.
dhp255.title: dhp255

dhp256.text:
You don’t become just
by passing hasty judgment.
An astute person evaluates both
what is pertinent and what is irrelevant.
dhp256.title: 19. The Just

dhp257.text:
A wise one judges others without haste,
justly and impartially;
that guardian of the law
is said to be just.
dhp257.title: dhp257

dhp258.text:
You’re not an astute scholar
just because you speak a lot.
One who is secure, free of enmity and fear,
is said to be astute.
dhp258.title: dhp258

dhp259.text:
You’re not one who has memorized the teaching
just because you recite a lot.
Someone who directly sees the teaching
after hearing only a little
is truly one who has memorized the teaching,
for they can never forget it.
dhp259.title: dhp259

dhp260.title: dhp260

dhp261.text:
One who is truthful and principled,
harmless, restrained, and self-controlled,
attentive, purged of stains,
is said to be a senior.
dhp261.title: dhp261

dhp262.text:
Not by mere enunciation,
or a beautiful complexion
does a person become holy,
if they’re jealous, stingy, and devious.
dhp262.title: dhp262

dhp263.text:
But if they’ve cut that out,
dug it up at the root, eradicated it,
that intelligent one, purged of vice,
is said to be holy.
dhp263.title: dhp263

dhp264.text:
A liar and breaker of vows is no ascetic
just because they shave their head.
How on earth can one be an ascetic
who’s full of desire and greed?
dhp264.title: dhp264

dhp265.text:
One who stops all wicked deeds,
great and small,
because of stopping wicked deeds
is said to be an ascetic.
dhp265.title: dhp265

dhp266.text:
You don’t become a mendicant
just by begging from others.
One who has undertaken domestic duties
has not yet become a mendicant.
dhp266.title: dhp266

dhp267.text:
But one living a spiritual life,
who has banished both merit and evil,
who wanders having appraised the world,
is said to be a mendicant.
dhp267.title: dhp267

dhp268.text:
You don’t become a sage by being sagelike,
while still confused and ignorant.
The astute one who holds the scales,
taking only the best,
dhp268.title: dhp268

dhp269.text:
and shunning the bad—
that is a sage, <j>and that is how one becomes a sage.
One who sagely weighs both in the world,
is thereby said to be a sage.
dhp269.title: dhp269

dhp270.text:
You don’t become a noble one
by harming living beings.
One harmless toward all living beings
is said to be a noble one.
dhp270.title: dhp270

dhp271.text:
Not by precepts and observances,
nor by much learning,
nor by meditative immersion,
nor by living in seclusion,
dhp271.title: dhp271

dhp272.text:
do I experience the bliss of renunciation
not frequented by ordinary people.
A mendicant cannot rest confident
without attaining the end of defilements.
dhp272.title: dhp272

dhp273.title: 20. The Path

dhp274.text: This is the path, there is no other for the purification of vision. You all must practice this, it is the way to baffle Māra.
dhp274.title: dhp274

dhp275.text:
When you all are practicing this,
you’ll make an end of suffering.
I have explained the path to you
for extracting the thorn with wisdom.
dhp275.title: dhp275

dhp276.text:
You yourselves must do the work,
the Realized Ones just show the way.
Meditators practicing absorption
are released from Māra’s bonds.
dhp276.title: dhp276

dhp277.text:
All conditions are impermanent—
when this is seen with wisdom,
one grows disillusioned with suffering:
this is the path to purity.
dhp277.title: dhp277

dhp280.text:
They don’t get going when it’s time to start;
they’re young and strong, but given to sloth.
Their mind depressed in sunken thought,
lazy and slothful, they can’t discern the path.
dhp280.title: dhp280

dhp281.text:
Guarded in speech, restrained in mind,
doing no unskillful bodily deed.
Purify these three ways of performing deeds,
and win the path known to seers.
dhp281.title: dhp281

dhp282.text:
From meditation springs wisdom,
without meditation, wisdom ends.
Knowing these two paths—
of progress and decline—
you should conduct yourself
so that wisdom grows.
dhp282.title: dhp282

dhp283.text:
Cut down the jungle, not just a tree;
from the jungle springs fear.
Having cut down jungle and snarl,
be free of jungles, mendicants!
dhp283.title: dhp283

dhp284.text:
So long as the vine, no matter how small,
that ties a man to women is not cut,
his mind remains trapped,
like a calf suckling its mother.
dhp284.title: dhp284

dhp285.text:
Cut out affection for oneself,
like plucking an autumn lotus.
Foster only the path to peace,
the extinguishment the Holy One taught.
dhp285.title: dhp285

dhp286.title: dhp286

dhp287.text:
As a mighty flood sweeps away a sleeping village,
death steals away a man
who dotes on children and cattle,
his mind caught up in them.
dhp287.title: dhp287

dhp288.text:
Children provide you no shelter,
nor does father, nor relatives.
When you’re seized by the terminator,
there’s no shelter in family.
dhp288.title: dhp288

dhp289.text:
Knowing the reason for this,
astute, and ethically restrained,
one would quickly clear the path
that leads to extinguishment.
dhp289.title: dhp289

dhp290.text:
If by giving up material happiness
one sees abundant happiness,
the attentive would give up material happiness,
seeing the abundant happiness.
dhp290.title: 21. Miscellaneous

dhp291.text:
Seeking their own happiness
by imposing suffering on others,
intimate with enmity,
they’re not freed from enmity.
dhp291.title: dhp291

dhp292.text:
They dump what should be done,
and do what should not be done.
For the insolent and the negligent,
their defilements only grow.
dhp292.title: dhp292

dhp293.text:
Those that have properly undertaken
constant mindfulness of the body,
don’t cultivate what should not be done,
but always do what should be done.
Mindful and aware,
their defilements come to an end.
dhp293.title: dhp293

dhp294.text:
Having slain mother and father,
and two aristocratic kings,
and having wiped out <j>the kingdom with its tax collector,
the brahmin walks on untroubled.
dhp294.title: dhp294

dhp295.text:
Having slain mother and father,
and two prosperous kings,
and a tiger as the fifth,
the brahmin walks on untroubled.
dhp295.title: dhp295

dhp296.text:
The disciples of Gotama
always wake up refreshed,
who day and night
constantly recollect the Buddha.
dhp296.title: dhp296

dhp300.text:
The disciples of Gotama
always wake up refreshed,
whose minds day and night
delight in harmlessness.
dhp300.title: dhp300

dhp302.text:
Going forth is hard, it’s hard to be happy;
life at home is hard too, and painful,
it’s painful to stay when you’ve nothing in common.
A traveler is a prey to pain,
so don’t be a traveler,
don’t be prey to pain.
dhp302.title: dhp302

dhp303.text:
One who is faithful, accomplished in ethics,
blessed with fame and wealth,
is honored in whatever place
they frequent.
dhp303.title: dhp303

dhp304.text:
The good shine from afar,
like the Himalayan peaks,
but the wicked are not seen,
like arrows scattered in the night.
dhp304.title: dhp304

dhp305.text:
Sitting alone, sleeping alone,
tirelessly wandering alone;
one who tames themselves alone
would delight within a forest.
dhp305.title: dhp305

dhp306.text:
A liar goes to hell,
as does one who denies what they did.
Both are equal in the hereafter,
those men of base deeds.
dhp306.title: 22. Hell

dhp307.text:
Many who wear a scrap of ocher cloth
are unrestrained and wicked.
Being wicked, they are reborn in hell
due to their bad deeds.
dhp307.title: dhp307

dhp308.text:
It’d be better for the immoral and unrestrained
to eat an iron ball,
scorching, like a burning flame,
than to eat the nation’s alms.
dhp308.title: dhp308

dhp309.text:
Four things befall a heedless man
who sleeps with another’s wife:
wickedness, poor sleep,
ill-repute, and rebirth in hell.
dhp309.title: dhp309

dhp310.text:
He accrues wickedness and is reborn in a bad place,
all so a frightened couple <j>may snatch a moment’s pleasure,
for which rulers impose a heavy punishment.
That’s why a man should not <j>sleep with another’s wife.
dhp310.title: dhp310

dhp311.text:
When kusa grass is wrongly grasped
it only cuts the hand.
So too, the ascetic life, when wrongly taken,
drags you to hell.
dhp311.title: dhp311

dhp312.text:
Any lax act,
any corrupt observance,
or suspicious spiritual life,
is not very fruitful.
dhp312.title: dhp312

dhp313.text:
If one is to do what should be done,
one should staunchly strive.
For the life gone forth when laxly led
just stirs up dust all the more.
dhp313.title: dhp313

dhp314.text:
A bad deed is better left undone,
for it will plague you later on.
A good deed is better done,
one that does not plague you.
dhp314.title: dhp314

dhp315.text:
As a frontier city
is guarded inside and out,
so you should ward yourselves—
don’t let the moment pass you by.
For if you miss your moment
you’ll grieve when sent to hell.
dhp315.title: dhp315

dhp316.text:
Unashamed of what is shameful,
ashamed of what is not shameful;
beings who uphold wrong view
go to a bad place.
dhp316.title: dhp316

dhp317.text:
Seeing danger where there is none,
and blind to the actual danger,
beings who uphold wrong view
go to a bad place.
dhp317.title: dhp317

dhp319.text:
Knowing a fault as a fault
and the faultless as faultless,
beings who uphold right view
go to a good place.
dhp319.title: dhp319

dhp320.text:
Like an elephant struck
with arrows in battle,
I shall endure abuse,
for so many folk are badly behaved.
dhp320.title: 23. Elephants

dhp321.title: dhp321

dhp322.text:
Those who have tamed themselves are better
than fine tamed mules,
thoroughbreds from Sindh,
or giant tuskers.
dhp322.title: dhp322

dhp323.text:
For not on those mounts
would you go to the untrodden place,
whereas, with the help of one <j>whose self is well tamed,
you go there, tamed by the tamed.
dhp323.title: dhp323

dhp324.text:
The tusker named Dhanapāla
is musky in rut, hard to control.
Bound, he eats not a morsel,
for he misses the elephant forest.
dhp324.title: dhp324

dhp325.text:
One who gets drowsy from overeating,
fond of sleep, rolling round the bed
like a great hog stuffed with grain:
that dullard returns to the womb again and again.
dhp325.title: dhp325

dhp326.text:
In the past my mind wandered
how it wished, where it liked, as it pleased.
Now I’ll carefully guide it,
as a trainer with a hook guides a rutting elephant.
dhp326.title: dhp326

dhp327.text:
Delight in diligence!
Take good care of your mind!
Pull yourself out of this pit,
like an elephant sunk in a bog.
dhp327.title: dhp327

dhp328.text:
If you find an alert companion,
an attentive friend to live happily together,
then, overcoming all adversities,
wander with them, joyful and mindful.
dhp328.title: dhp328

dhp329.text:
If you find no alert companion,
no attentive friend to live happily together,
then, like a king who flees his conquered realm,
wander alone like a tusker in the wilds.
dhp329.title: dhp329

dhp330.text:
It’s better to wander alone,
there’s no fellowship with fools.
Wander alone and do no wrong,
at ease like a tusker in the wilds.
dhp330.title: dhp330

dhp331.title: dhp331

dhp332.text:
In this world it’s a blessing to serve
one’s mother and one’s father.
And it’s a blessing also to serve
ascetics and brahmins.
dhp332.title: dhp332

dhp333.title: dhp333

dhp33.text:
The mind quivers and quakes,
hard to guard, hard to curb.
The discerning straighten it out,
like a fletcher an arrow.
dhp33.title: 3. The Mind

dhp34.text:
Like a fish pulled from the sea
and cast upon the shore,
this mind flounders about,
trying to throw off Māra’s dominion.
dhp34.title: dhp34

dhp35.title: dhp35

dhp36.text:
So hard to see, so subtle,
alighting where it will;
the discerning protect the mind,
a guarded mind leads to bliss.
dhp36.title: dhp36

dhp37.text:
The mind travels far, wandering alone;
incorporeal, it lies hidden in the heart.
Those who will restrain the mind
are freed from Māra’s bonds.
dhp37.title: dhp37

dhp38.text:
Those of unsteady mind,
who don’t understand the true teaching,
and whose confidence wavers,
do not perfect their wisdom.
dhp38.title: dhp38

dhp39.text:
One whose mind is not festering,
whose heart is undamaged,
who’s given up right and wrong,
alert, has nothing to fear.
dhp39.title: dhp39

dhp40.text:
Knowing this body breaks like a pot,
and fortifying the mind like a citadel,
attack Māra with the sword of wisdom,
guard your conquest, and never settle.
dhp40.title: dhp40

dhp41.text:
All too soon this body
will lie upon the earth,
bereft of consciousness,
tossed aside like a worthless log.
dhp41.title: dhp41

dhp43.text:
A rightly directed mind
would do you more good
than your mother or father
or any other relative.
dhp43.title: dhp43

dhp334.text:
When a man lives heedlessly,
craving grows in them like a camel’s foot creeper.
They jump from one thing to the next, like a langur
greedy for fruit in a forest grove.
dhp334.title: 24. Craving

dhp335.text:
Whoever is beaten by this wretched craving,
this attachment to the world,
their sorrow grows,
like grass in the rain.
dhp335.title: dhp335

dhp336.text:
But whoever prevails over this wretched craving,
so hard to get over in the world,
their sorrows fall from them,
like a drop from a lotus-leaf.
dhp336.title: dhp336

dhp337.text:
I say this to you, good people,
all those who have gathered here:
dig up the root of craving,
as you’d dig up grass in search of roots.
Don’t let Māra break you again and again,
like a stream breaking a reed.
dhp337.title: dhp337

dhp338.text:
A tree grows back even when cut down,
so long as its roots are strong and undamaged;
suffering springs up again and again,
so long as the tendency to craving is not pulled out.
dhp338.title: dhp338

dhp339.text:
A person of low views
in whom the thirty-six streams
that flow to pleasure are mighty,
is swept away by lustful thoughts.
dhp339.title: dhp339

dhp340.text:
The streams flow everywhere;
a weed springs up and remains.
Seeing this weed that has been born,
cut the root with wisdom.
dhp340.title: dhp340

dhp341.text:
A personage’s joys
flow from senses and cravings.
Seekers of happiness, bent on pleasure,
continue to be reborn and grow old.
dhp341.title: dhp341

dhp342.text:
People governed by thirst,
crawl about like a trapped rabbit.
Bound and fettered, for a long time
they return to pain time and again.
dhp342.title: dhp342

dhp343.text:
People governed by thirst,
crawl about like a trapped rabbit.
That’s why one who longs for dispassion
should dispel thirst.
dhp343.title: dhp343

dhp344.text:
Unsnarled, they set out for the jungle,
then they run right back to the jungle they left behind.
Just look at this individual!
Freed, they run to bondage.
dhp344.title: dhp344

dhp345.text:
The attentive say that shackle is not strong
that’s made of iron, wood, or knots.
But obsession with jeweled earrings,
concern for your partners and children:
dhp345.title: dhp345

dhp346.text:
this, say the attentive, is a strong shackle
dragging the indulgent down, hard to escape.
Having cut this one too they go forth,
unconcerned, having given up sensual pleasures.
dhp346.title: dhp346

dhp347.text:
Besotted by lust they fall into the stream,
like a spider caught in the web she wove.
The attentive proceed, having cut this one too,
unconcerned, having given up all suffering.
dhp347.title: dhp347

dhp348.text:
Let go of the past, let go of the future,
let go of the present, having gone beyond rebirth.
With your heart freed in every respect,
you’ll not come again to rebirth and old age.
dhp348.title: dhp348

dhp349.text:
For a personage churned by thoughts,
very lustful, focusing on beauty,
their craving grows and grows,
tying them with a stout bond.
dhp349.title: dhp349

dhp350.text:
But one who loves to calm their thoughts,
developing perception of ugliness, ever mindful,
will surely eliminate that craving,
cutting off the bonds of Māra.
dhp350.title: dhp350

dhp351.text:
One who is confident, unafraid,
rid of craving, free of blemish,
having struck down the arrows flying to future lives,
this bag of bones is their last.
dhp351.title: dhp351

dhp352.text:
Rid of craving, free of grasping,
expert in the definition of terms,
knowing the correct
structure and sequence of syllables,
they are said to be one who bears their final body,
one of great wisdom, a great person.
dhp352.title: dhp352

dhp353.text:
I am the vanquisher of all, the knower of all,
unsullied in the midst of all things.
I’ve given up all, freed in the ending of craving.
Since I know for myself, whose follower should I be?
dhp353.title: dhp353

dhp354.title: dhp354

dhp355.text:
Riches ruin a simpleton,
but not a seeker of the far shore.
From craving for wealth, a simpleton
ruins themselves and others.
dhp355.title: dhp355

dhp356.text:
Weeds are the bane of crops,
but greed is these folk’s bane.
That’s why a gift to one rid of greed
is so very fruitful.
dhp356.title: dhp356

dhp360.title: 25. Mendicants

dhp361.title: dhp361

dhp362.text:
One restrained in hand and foot,
and in speech, the supreme restraint;
happy inside, serene,
solitary, content, I call a mendicant.
dhp362.title: dhp362

dhp363.text:
When a mendicant of restrained mouth,
thoughtful in counsel, not restless,
explains the text and its meaning,
their words are sweet.
dhp363.title: dhp363

dhp364.text:
Delighting in the teaching, enjoying the teaching,
contemplating the teaching,
a mendicant who recollects the teaching
doesn’t fall away from the true teaching.
dhp364.title: dhp364

dhp365.text:
A well-off mendicant ought not look down
on others, nor should they be envious.
A mendicant who envies others
does not achieve immersion.
dhp365.title: dhp365

dhp366.text:
If a mendicant is poor in offerings,
the well-to-do ought not look down on them.
For the gods indeed praise them,
who are tireless and pure of livelihood.
dhp366.title: dhp366

dhp367.text:
One who has no sense of ownership
in the whole realm of name and form,
who does not grieve for that which is not,
is said to be a mendicant.
dhp367.title: dhp367

dhp368.text:
A mendicant who meditates on love,
devoted to the Buddha’s teaching,
would realize the peaceful state,
the blissful stilling of conditions.
dhp368.title: dhp368

dhp369.text:
Bail out this boat, mendicant!
When bailed out it will float lightly.
Having cut off desire and hate,
you shall reach extinguishment.
dhp369.title: dhp369

dhp370.text:
Five to cut, five to drop,
and five more to develop.
When a mendicant slips five chains
they’re said to have crossed the flood.
dhp370.title: dhp370

dhp371.text:
Practice absorption, don’t be negligent!
Don’t let the mind delight in the senses!
Don’t heedlessly swallow a hot iron ball!
And when it burns, don’t cry, “Oh, the pain!”
dhp371.title: dhp371

dhp372.text:
No absorption for one without wisdom,
no wisdom for one without absorption.
But one with absorption and wisdom—
they have truly drawn near to extinguishment.
dhp372.title: dhp372

dhp373.text:
A mendicant who enters an empty hut
with mind at peace
finds a superhuman delight
as they rightly discern the Dhamma.
dhp373.title: dhp373

dhp374.text:
Whenever they are mindful
of the rise and fall of the aggregates,
they feel rapture and joy:
that is freedom from death for one who knows.
dhp374.title: dhp374

dhp375.text:
This is the very start of the path
for a wise mendicant here:
guarding the senses, contentment,
and restraint in the monastic code.
dhp375.title: dhp375

dhp376.text:
Mix with spiritual friends,
who are tireless and pure of livelihood.
Share what you have with others,
being skillful in your conduct.
And when you’re full of joy,
you’ll make an end to suffering.
dhp376.title: dhp376

dhp377.text:
As a jasmine sheds
its withered flowers,
O mendicants,
shed greed and hate.
dhp377.title: dhp377

dhp378.text:
Calm in body, calm in speech,
peaceful and serene;
a mendicant who’s spat out the world’s bait
is said to be one at peace.
dhp378.title: dhp378

dhp379.text:
Urge yourself on,
reflect on yourself.
A mendicant self-controlled and mindful
will always dwell in happiness.
dhp379.title: dhp379

dhp380.text:
Self is indeed the lord of self,
for who else would be one’s lord?
Self is indeed the home of self,
so restrain yourself,
as a merchant his thoroughbred steed.
dhp380.title: dhp380

dhp381.text:
A monk full of joy
trusting in the Buddha’s teaching,
would realize the peaceful state,
the blissful stilling of conditions.
dhp381.title: dhp381

dhp382.text:
A young mendicant
devoted to the Buddha’s teaching,
shines upon this world,
like the moon freed from clouds.
dhp382.title: dhp382

dhp383.text:
Cut the stream, striving!
Cast aside sensual pleasures, brahmin.
Knowing the ending of conditions,
know the uncreated, brahmin.
dhp383.title: 26. Brahmins

dhp384.text:
When a brahmin has gone beyond
dualistic phenomena,
then they consciously
make an end of all fetters.
dhp384.title: dhp384

dhp385.text:
One for whom there is no crossing over
or crossing back, or crossing over and back;
stress-free, detached,
that’s who I declare a brahmin.
dhp385.title: dhp385

dhp386.text:
Absorbed, rid of hopes,
their task completed, without defilements,
arrived at the highest goal:
that’s who I declare a brahmin.
dhp386.title: dhp386

dhp387.text:
The sun blazes by day,
the moon radiates at night,
the aristocrat shines in armor,
and the brahmin shines in absorption.
But all day and all night,
the Buddha blazes with glory.
dhp387.title: dhp387

dhp388.text:
A brahmin’s so-called <j>since they’ve banished evil,
an ascetic’s so-called <j>since they live a serene life.
One who has renounced all stains
is said to be a “renunciant”.
dhp388.title: dhp388

dhp389.text:
One should never strike a brahmin,
nor should a brahmin retaliate.
Woe to the one who hurts a brahmin,
and woe for the one who retaliates.
dhp389.title: dhp389

dhp390.text:
Nothing is better for a brahmin
than to hold their mind back from attachment.
From wherever a cruel wish recoils,
right there suffering subsides.
dhp390.title: dhp390

dhp391.text:
Who does nothing wrong
by body, speech or mind,
restrained in these three respects,
that’s who I declare a brahmin.
dhp391.title: dhp391

dhp392.text:
You should graciously honor
the one from whom you learn the Dhamma
taught by the awakened Buddha,
as a brahmin honors the sacred flame.
dhp392.title: dhp392

dhp393.text:
Not by matted hair or family,
or birth is one a brahmin.
Those who are  truthful and principled:
they are pure, they are brahmins.
dhp393.title: dhp393

dhp394.text:
Why the matted hair, you simpleton,
and why the skin of deer?
The tangle is inside you,
yet you polish up your outsides.
dhp394.title: dhp394

dhp395.text:
A personage who wears robes of rags,
lean, their limbs showing veins,
meditating alone in the forest,
that’s who I declare a brahmin.
dhp395.title: dhp395

dhp396.text:
I don’t call someone a brahmin
after the mother’s womb they’re born from.
If they still have attachments,
they’re just someone who says “worthy”.
Having nothing, taking nothing:
that’s who I declare a brahmin.
dhp396.title: dhp396

dhp397.text:
Having cut off all fetters
they have no anxiety.
They’ve slipped their chains and are detached:
that’s who I declare a brahmin.
dhp397.title: dhp397

dhp398.text:
They’ve cut the strap and harness,
the halter and bridle too,
with cross-bar lifted, they’re awakened:
that’s who I declare a brahmin.
dhp398.title: dhp398

dhp399.text:
Abuse, killing, caging:
they endure these without anger.
Patience is their powerful army:
that’s who I declare a brahmin.
dhp399.title: dhp399
